data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'n-t-y', meaning 'mother'. It symbolizes the deep bond between a mother and her child. Parents who choose Mutia usually hope their child will grow to embody mother's love and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: In many Islamic communities, the name "Mutia" holds significant cultural importance as it highlights the strong bond between a mother and her child. It is a name that evokes the deep love, care, and nurturing that is expected from a mother in Islamic culture. This name can also be given as a tribute to a beloved grandmother, reminding us of the sacrifices and endless love that grandmothers exhibit towards their families.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, the name "Mutia" can represent the concept of divine motherhood. Allah, the one and only God, is referred to as the 'Mother' of all believers in various Islamic traditions. The Hadith of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) states, "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibreel to him and says: 'What is My servant doing?' Jibreel goes and finds him doing such and such an action, and Allah says: 'My servant is doing what I love, so let Me be pleased with him.' post which Allah makes a covenant with the servant, and Allah becomes his 'Rasheed' (guide to the right path) and He becomes, for him, his 'Mother.'"[1] Thus, the name "Mutia" symbolizes the nurturing, guiding, and loving nature of Allah towards His servants.
